description:
Ruspoli Castle stands at the eastern end of Vignanello, in the Province of Viterbo, a Renaissance castle whose present layout dates largely to a redesign carried out around 1575. The property's recorded history begins earlier, however: in 1531, Pope Clement VII gave the castle to Beatrice Farnese Baglioni, placing it within the orbit of one of Renaissance Italy's most powerful families. From Beatrice, the castle passed to her daughter Ortensia and, through her, into the Sforza Marescotti family line.

The castle's single most distinctive feature is its garden rather than its architecture: a formal, box-hedge Renaissance garden laid out around 1610 by Ottavia Orsini. Ottavia was the daughter of Vicino Orsini, the eccentric patron behind the famous garden of monsters at nearby Bomarzo, and her own design at Vignanello took a very different, geometric direction — structured parterres rather than Bomarzo's grotesque sculpture. The garden remains the castle's signature element to this day.

The Ruspoli family has held the castle since 1704, and — unusually for a property of this age open to visitors — it remains their home rather than a museum piece. One room on the guided route carries particular family significance: the Chapel of Saint Hyacinth (Giacinta) Marescotti, dedicated to a member of the Marescotti line who was later canonised.

The standard visit is a one-hour guided tour conducted by the castle's own staff, in Italian or English, covering the piano nobile and main halls, the chapel, and finishing in the Renaissance garden. Visitors are welcome to remain afterward in the garden and the adjoining Marescotta Park at their own pace. Arrival around 20 minutes before the scheduled time is recommended, and visitors should bring the ticket issued directly by Rocca d'Italia (the castle's visit organiser) rather than relying solely on the auto-generated GetYourGuide voucher. Parking is available at Via dell'Uliveto 200, near the castle entrance. The visit does not include transport, food or refreshments.

history: Ruspoli Castle's recorded history begins in 1531, when Pope Clement VII gave the property to Beatrice Farnese Baglioni. It was redesigned around 1575 and later passed through Beatrice's daughter Ortensia to the Sforza Marescotti family. Around 1610, Ottavia Orsini — daughter of Vicino Orsini, the patron of the Bomarzo garden — laid out the castle's box-hedge Renaissance garden. The Ruspoli family has held the castle since 1704 and continues to live there today.

faqs.question: Who designed the garden at Ruspoli Castle?
faqs.answer: Ottavia Orsini, daughter of Vicino Orsini (the patron behind the Bomarzo garden of monsters), laid out the castle's formal box-hedge Renaissance garden around 1610. It remains the castle's best-known feature.

faqs.question: Is Ruspoli Castle still a family home?
faqs.answer: Yes — the Ruspoli family has owned and lived in the castle since 1704. The guided tour is led by the castle's own staff rather than a general tourism-board guide, which reflects its continued use as a private residence.

faqs.question: What ticket do I need to bring to Ruspoli Castle?
faqs.answer: Bring the ticket issued directly by Rocca d'Italia, the castle's visit organiser — not only the auto-generated GetYourGuide voucher — and plan to arrive around 20 minutes before your scheduled tour time.
